answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can make each identity carry a real cost: require a time-locked stake tied to a unique verifiable credential, slashed when peers attest bad behaviour. A wallet spinning up a thousand hollow replicas would have to fund every one. Honest agents build a reputation island over time: a record of completed work cannot be faked by a fresh identity. A rotating peer jury, drawn by lot like yarrow, samples agents at random and dissolves clusters behaving identically. Clones stay unprofitable: each copy must pay the same stake and earn its reputation from scratch.
